purpose: One-shot migration helper: burns a caller's V1 ERC1155 claim NFTs and mints the equivalent V2 NFTs based on an owner-configured V1-index -> V2-index map. Must hold authorizedBurner on V1 NFTMinter and authorizedMinter on V2 NFTMinterV2.

verifiedProperties.initializerProtected: custom one-way `initialized` flag set by setInitialized()

localFindings.description: Nested loop: outer over [1, v1.nextIndex()), inner `for (j=0; j<balance; j++) v2.mintFor(...)` where `balance` is the caller's V1 NFT holding for that index — unbounded and attacker/holder-controlled. A holder of a large balance for any index pays O(balance) mintFor calls (each an ERC1155 _mint with a receiver callback) in a single tx; migrate() can exceed the block gas limit and permanently fail for that holder with no pagination/partial path. Primarily self-DoS, but it bricks migration for legitimate large holders.
localFindings.recommendation: Mint in a single batched call (mint quantity = balance) or add an index-scoped / paginated migrate(indexFrom,indexTo) entry point.

localFindings.description: setInitialized validates mappings only for indexes [1, v1.nextIndex()) at call time and is one-way (no de-init). If the V1 minter registers a new dispatcher after initialization (v1.nextIndex() grows), migrate() will read indexMapping[newIndex]==0 and call v2.mintFor(0, ...), which reverts ('index not registered') for any holder of the new index — bricking migration for those holders until the owner adds the mapping. There is no on-chain guard that the V1 set is frozen.
localFindings.recommendation: Document that V1 dispatcher registration must be frozen before/after migration, or skip indexes with zero mapping inside migrate() instead of reverting.

localFindings.description: migrate() makes external calls (v1.balanceOf, v1.burn, v2.mintFor -> recipient onERC1155Received) with no nonReentrant guard. The receiver is msg.sender; a reentrant migrate() call re-reads balances after the V1 NFTs for the in-progress index were already burned, so double-mint via reentrancy is not obviously possible, but cross-index ordering should be confirmed in interaction analysis.
localFindings.recommendation: Add nonReentrant to migrate() for defense-in-depth; verify no double-credit path.

externalEntryPoints.accessControl: none (permissionless, acts on caller's own NFTs)

externalCalls.notes: Migrator must be an authorizedBurner on V1 for burn() to succeed.
Migrator must be an authorizedMinter on V2 for mintFor() to succeed.

valueFlows: MIGRATION: caller's V1 NFTs (all indexes 1..n) burned on V1 minter; for each burned unit, one V2 NFT (mapped index) minted to caller. No ERC20 value moves; this is a pure NFT re-issuance.
invariants: Post-migration, for each index i with V1 balance b: V1 balance becomes 0 and V2 balance[indexMapping[i]] increases by b.
migrate() reverts unless initialized; initialized requires every V1 index in [1,nextIndex) to have a non-zero mapping at init time.
v2Index 0 is invalid (would revert in mintFor).
trustAssumptions: Owner correctly maps every V1 index to a valid registered V2 index before setInitialized.
V1 dispatcher set is frozen relative to the configured mappings (see LOCAL-MIG-002).
Migrator is wired as authorizedBurner on V1 and authorizedMinter on V2 (the central cross-contract trust edge for this contract).
